newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-LIPINSKI STAYS ON COURSE FOR CROWN.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-LIPINSKI STAYS ON COURSE FOR CROWN.

text.p: Tara Lipinski continued her express run towards the title of youngest-ever world figure skating champion on Friday.

But while 14-year-old Lipinski maintained the imperious form she has shown for the past month, title-holder and fellow American Michelle Kwan messed up her combination jump in the short programme and finished fourth.
Nicole Bobek, skating a day after the death of her coach, Carlo Fassi, was accompanied by Fassi's widow Christa, yet still seemed to be overtaken by her sorrow.
The American over-rotated her opening triple lutz and put both hands and one knee down landing a triple toe loop as she placed eighth.
China's 1995 champion Chen Lu, completely out of form after missing four months of training, failed in her objective of qualifying for next winter's Olympics in Japan by finishing 25th..
That was one place below what she needed to guarantee Olympic qualification. She will now need a skate-off later in the year to make the Nagano Games.
Vanessa Gusmeroli of France was second from Russian Maria Butyrskaya with Hungarian Krisztina Czako and European champion Irina Slutskaya of Russia fifth and sixth.

"I was pleased to do a clean short because I messed it up last year and this has given me a lot of confidence," said Lipinski, who has relieved Kwan of both the U.S. and Champions Series titles over the past month.
"But I am not expecting to win at all. I think if I thought I could win this it would put too much pressure on me."
